in_arabic.name: يوسف
in_arabic.long_meaning: يوسف هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و معناه: الشخص الصالح والبار، المطيع لله. وهو أحد الأنبياء في الإسلام، ورد ذكره في القرآن الكريم في سورة يوسف، وهو مشتق من الجذر اللغوي 'ي-و-س-ف' الذي يعني: 'الصبر' و'الشد' و'المنع'. وقد ورد اسم يوسف في القرآن الكريم 34 مرة، وهو من الأسماء التي تحمل دلالات روحانية و دينية كبيرة في الثقافة الإسلامية.

in_urdu.name: یوسف
in_urdu.meaning: یوسف کا مطلب ہے اچھا اور فرمانبردار شخص
in_urdu.long_meaning: یوسف ایک مذکر نام ہے جو عربی زبان سے نکلا ہے۔ اس کا مطلب ہے اچھا اور فرمانبردار شخص، جو اللہ کے فرمانوں کا پابند ہے۔ یہ نام قرآن مجید میں سورة یوسف میں ذکر کیا گیا ہے، جو اسلامی ثقافت میں ایک مقدس نام ہے۔ اس نام کی اصلی عربی جڑ 'ی-و-س-ف' ہے، جو 'صبر'، 'شد' اور 'منع' کے معنی رکھتی ہے۔

in_hindi.name: यूसुफ
in_hindi.meaning: यूसुफ का अर्थ है अच्छा और परमेश्वर का आज्ञाकारी व्यक्ति
in_hindi.long_meaning: यूसुफ एक पुल्लिंग नाम है जो अरबी भाषा से आया है। इसका अर्थ है अच्छा और परमेश्वर का आज्ञाकारी व्यक्ति, जो ईश्वर के आदेशों का पालन करता है। यह नाम कुरआन में सूरत यूसुफ में उल्लिखित है, जो इस्लामी संस्कृति में एक पवित्र नाम है। इसकी मूल अरबी जड़ 'य-व-स-फ' है, जिसका अर्थ है 'धैर्य', 'कठिनाई' और 'निषेध'।

in_pashto.name: یوسف
in_pashto.meaning: یوسف د ښه او د خدای فرمانبردار سړي نوم دی
in_pashto.long_meaning: یوسف یو مذکر نوم دی چی د عربي ژبې نه اخیستل شوی دی. ددی نوم مطلب دی ښه او د خدای فرمانبردار سړی، هغه کسي چی د الهي حکمونه مني. دا نوم د قرآن کریم په سورت یوسف کی ذکر شوی دی، چی دی د افغانستان د اسلامی کلتور په کی د يو سپیڅلي نوم څخه ګڼل کيږي. ددی نوم اصلی عربی ريښه 'ی-و-س-ف' ده، چی د 'صبر'، 'شد' او 'منع' په معنی دی.

in_english.name: Youcef
in_english.meaning: Good, obedient person, derived from Arabic roots
in_english.long_meaning: Youcef, also spelled Yusuf, is a masculine given name originating from Arabic. It means 'good' or 'obedient person', signifying one who adheres to God's commandments. Mentioned in the Quran, specifically in Surah Yusuf, this name holds significant spiritual and religious connotations in Islamic tradition. Etymologically derived from the Arabic root 'y-w-s-f', it relates to concepts of 'patience', 'hardship', and 'restraint'. The name Youcef has been historically significant across various Muslim cultures and continues to be a popular choice for newborns.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Youcef" (or "Hosea" in English) holds a significant cultural impact within the Islamic tradition, particularly due to its mention in the Quran in Surah Al-Anbiya' (The Prophets) in the context of prophetic stories. In numerous historical and literary sources, Youcef is described as a righteous and wise leader who was sent to the city of Nineveh to call its people to repentance and turn away from sin. His story illustrates the mercy and forgiveness of God towards those who truly repent and return to Him, even after great sins and misdeeds.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Youcef" can be found in its connection to the prophets and their roles as messengers of God's mercy and guidance to humanity. The name serves as a reminder of the importance of righteous leadership and the power of repentance and forgiveness. It also underscores the prophetic tradition of calling people to return to their faith and live virtuous lives, as should be the model for all Muslims. By embracing the spiritual meaning of the name, individuals can strive to become better leaders and followers in their own communities, emulating the virtues of Youcef and other prophets.

historical_references.reference: Youcef is considered a prophet in both the Islamic and Jewish traditions, known as 'Hosea' in the Hebrew Bible. He is the son of Prophet Saba (Sheba) and is a descendant of King David. According to the Quran, Prophet Youcef was falsely accused of theft by his brothers and was thrown into a well, but was saved by a fisherman. Later, he was sold as a slave to Egypt, where he became a trusted servant to the King of Egypt, who eventually appointed him as his vizier. Youcef's wisdom and good deeds won the admiration of the people, and he was eventually reunited with his family.

historical_references.reference: Youcef's story is also retold in the Islamic tradition as one of the 'Stories of the Prophets' in the Quran, and is a popular subject in Islamic art and literature. It is a reminder of the importance of faith, trust in Allah, and the triumph of good over evil.
